lessons.title: Pests and problems to look for
lessons.html:
What scouting is

Scouting means walking through the orchard on a set plan and checking trees for pests, diseases and damage. A scout does not spray. A scout looks, counts and records, so the manager can decide if and when to act. Good scouting saves money, because the farm sprays only when it is needed and only where it is needed.

Main macadamia pests in South Africa

PestWhat you see
Stink bugs (including the two-spotted bug and green vegetable bug)Bugs on nuts and shoots; small sting marks on husks; later, damaged and spotted kernels
Macadamia nut borerSmall holes in the husk, frass (sawdust-like waste), larvae inside nuts
Litchi moth and other mothsHoles in nuts, larvae, early nut drop
ThripsDamaged, curled or scarred new leaves and flowers
MitesBronze or speckled leaves

Diseases and other problems

  • Husk rot and flower blight – brown, rotting flowers or husks after wet weather.
  • Phytophthora – bleeding or cracked bark near the base, thin canopy, yellow leaves.
  • Nutrient problems – yellowing or unusual leaf colours.
  • Water problems – wilting, or waterlogged soil.
  • Animal damage – rats, porcupines, monkeys and birds eating nuts or bark.

Natural enemies

Also record useful insects such as ladybirds, lacewings, predatory bugs and spiders. They eat pests. If many natural enemies are present, the manager may delay a spray.

Safety in the orchard

  • Check with the supervisor that no block has been sprayed recently before entering. Respect re-entry signs.
  • Watch for snakes and bees. Wear closed shoes and long trousers.
  • Carry water and a phone, and tell someone which blocks you are scouting.

lessons.title: Scouting method and recording
lessons.html:
Following a scouting plan

The farm sets a scouting method so that the numbers from week to week can be compared. You must follow the same method every time.

A typical method

  1. Get your scouting sheet or app, a hand lens, flagging tape, a knife and a sample bag.
  2. Go to the blocks on your list for the day. Walk the set route, often a zig-zag or a W pattern across the block, so you cover edges and centre.
  3. Stop at the set number of trees. Pick them evenly, not just the easy ones next to the road.
  4. On each tree, check the parts the method says: for example a set number of nut clusters, new shoots, flowers and the trunk base.
  5. Use a beating sheet or knock-down method if the farm uses one for stink bugs. Count the bugs that fall.
  6. Cut open a set number of nuts to look for borer larvae and sting damage when the method asks for it.
  7. Write down what you find for each tree straight away. Do not rely on memory.

Recording well

  • Record block, date, time, weather, tree number and the count for each pest.
  • Write zero when you find nothing. A blank is not the same as zero.
  • Note natural enemies and any disease or damage.
  • Mark hot spots with flagging tape and GPS or row numbers.
  • Take samples in a labelled bag if you cannot identify a pest.

Reporting

Hand in your sheets the same day. Report at once if a count is above the action level the farm has set, or if you see something new. The manager compares your counts with the action levels and decides on control. Honest, accurate counts are the most important part of the job.

Key points

  • Scouts look, count and record; the manager decides on control.
  • Follow the same route, tree numbers and checks every time.
  • Know the main pests: stink bugs, nut borer, moths, thrips and mites.
  • Record zeros and natural enemies, and mark hot spots.
  • Report high counts and new problems the same day.

quiz.question: What is the main job of a scout?

options.text: To spray every block each week
To look, count and record pests and problems

quiz.question: Which sign points to macadamia nut borer?

options.text: Small holes in the husk with frass

quiz.question: Why should you walk a zig-zag or W route through the block?

options.text: To cover both the edges and the centre of the block
To avoid the trees with pests
Because the road is in the middle

quiz.question: You check a tree and find no stink bugs. What should you record?

options.text: Write the count from last week

quiz.question: Why should you record natural enemies such as ladybirds and lacewings?

options.text: They eat pests, so the manager may delay a spray
They show the trees need water
